model.title: Strengthening the Rule of Law in the Brazilian Amazon Act
model.meta: Foreign Relations Committee · Sen. Timothy Kaine (D-VA)

summary.text: The bill would direct the US to help Brazil fight criminal networks behind illegal logging, mining, fishing and wildlife trade in the Brazilian Amazon, including through training, technical help and tracing of criminal funds. It would also ask the US International Development Finance Corporation to place a staff member in Brazil to look for viable economic opportunities in the region and report to Congress within 180 days. The bill would further have the State Department support local communities with lawful livelihoods and protected-area management, report annually for five years on progress, and report on drivers of deforestation such as commodity imports and China's role. Finally, it would ask the US Treasury to push international lenders such as the World Bank and IMF to oppose loans that worsen deforestation in the Amazon.
